decision: Added one immutable final-program snapshot and reused its body observations for the compatibility revision
why: The lookup key needs richer source and configuration authority without a second compiler-sized body walk
result: focused tests green

decision: Moved the target reuse decision before miss-only OCaml preparation

result: target work is not skipped yet; ordering contract passes

decision: Published a redacted request-scoped reuse report with explicit unfinished fields
why: Missing evidence must not look like zero cost or a successful cache
result: report fixture passes; no readiness change

decision: Introduced a bounded opaque in-memory catalog with leases, LRU eviction, reset, and quarantine
why: Future replay needs process-local storage without retaining Haxe typed objects or trusting mutable payload bytes
result: mechanics fixture passes; catalog remains observation-only

decision: Rejected an ordinary macro static as the physical cache owner
why: The actual Haxe 4.3.7 server fixture showed every warm request creating request sequence 1
result: root cause found; no disk-cache fallback introduced

decision: Used Haxe's public persistent macro-runtime marker only on catalog state
why: Upstream eval reinitializes ordinary statics but preserves fields marked persistent in the cached interpreter
result: exact repeat now survives in one realm

decision: Ignored only Haxe 4.3.7's zero-width compiler-owned keep marker on the selected main field
why: The server accumulated duplicate internal markers even though source, typed bodies, output, and behavior were unchanged; user metadata must remain revisioned
evidence: Reflaxe commits 16766aa2db6ad5f31e1bef0958adaf44bccf49e4 and e2f0f81a6e42de920d3fb01b93a3814aedd41fc3; upstream Haxe 4.3.7 src/typing/finalization.ml
result: cold and exact warm request revisions now match

decision: Allowed macro errors either to preserve or replace the interpreter realm, while requiring the next successful request to be exact and internally consistent
why: The actual upstream route preserved the realm for this handled macro failure; safety depends on exact keys and no failed-request admission, not mandatory replacement
result: full reset, error, NoMacroCache, classpath, and restart matrix passes

decision: Ran the clean target-reuse contract with no diagnostic-only callback
why: The permanent gate must prove production-shaped ownership rather than rely on the temporary declaration trace used for diagnosis
result: all catalog, contract, report, probe, and realm markers pass

decision: Confirmed all hxhx Oracle replies are integrated
why: Avoid losing architecture decisions delivered through chat instead of result files
result: Two current packets and one archived server review all map to committed checkpoints and Bead mutations; no outstanding reply found

decision: Closed generated-source runtime and native declaration authority conservatively
why: A packed candidate cannot be replay-safe while the artifact manifest reports incomplete ownership
evidence: OcamlSourceBundleAuthority; RuntimeCopier; real inspect/scaffold/build/run fixtures; runtime manifest and requirement fixtures
result: Generated source manifests now report completeForSourceBundle=true with zero blockers; external toolchain and Dune products remain fresh and uncached

decision: Use one self-validating packed source-bundle payload
why: Shadow replay must consume the exact opaque bytes a future catalog would retain, not request-local target objects.
evidence: OcamlSourceBundleCandidate packs a canonical plain-value index plus contiguous file bytes, self-decodes, validates paths/claims/authorities/ranges/digests/revision, and rejects corruption; focused contract passed.
result: Packed-candidate boundary complete; no catalog admission, replay, or target work skip enabled.

decision: Replay packed source only into a disposable private directory
why: The observation must prove reconstructed bytes and ownership before any production hit can publish output.
evidence: The real target-reuse fixture rebuilt receipt semantics and a fresh target manifest from the decoded payload, matched all stable files and the source-bundle revision, and left normal output as the only published tree.
result: Stable-source shadow replay complete; volatile evidence, diagnostics, memory, and broad failure/invalidation gates remain.

decision: Count candidate bytes exactly and enforce the real entry cap before replay
why: A bounded design must reject oversized source bundles and distinguish exact owned bytes from unavailable process-memory metrics.
evidence: Candidate packing rejects payloads above 64 MiB by default; the report exposes exact payload/index/catalog accounting and keeps RSS/GC explicitly null; focused contract passed.
result: Payload accounting and cap gate complete; external repeated-process RSS proof still remains.

decision: Run shadow replay through the existing full clean-versus-warm server matrix
why: A single happy-path report cannot prove invalidation, rollback, source-map freshness, native behavior, or retained-memory safety.
evidence: Complete-program server gate passed implementation/API edits, add/delete/move, classpath, defines/profiles/DCE, macros, malformed source, transaction failure, A-B-A, 30 repeats, source-map line edits, restart, native builds/runs; final RSS 504416 KiB versus 424864 KiB baseline and 497344 KiB after request 20.
result: Extended stable-source shadow and external RSS qualification passed; transient peak remains observational, not retained growth.

decision: Observe complete runtime and native-source inputs before miss-only preparation
why: The early key must not report source authority incomplete after the same request later proves a complete source bundle.
evidence: The probe now checks and revisions the full runtime source manifest, revisions native source declarations from final-program plus source configuration facts, reuses the checked runtime snapshot during copy, and keeps only missing exact target implementation identity as the baseline blocker; focused runtime/artifact/reuse gates passed.
result: Early source identity is complete; production remains fail-closed until an exact target implementation digest is supplied.

decision: Record exact early key construction time
why: Acceptance requires proof that lookup identity is cheaper than miss-only target generation
evidence: Reflaxe ec90501 adds lifecycle timing; target report contract passed with a non-negative measured value
result: The observation now separates key cost, target revision observation, miss preparation, and replay validation; no target work is skipped

decision: Keep the checked runtime manifest through output generation
why: Clearing it in onCompileStart happened after the early probe and forced a second load
evidence: Moved reset to filterTypes request start; target reuse contract passed
result: One request loads and verifies runtime inputs before key construction and later reuses the same snapshot

decision: Decode target payloads before replay and quarantine failures
why: The generic catalog intentionally stores opaque bytes, so target validation must fail closed before file publication
evidence: Candidate fixture admits valid bytes, leases and decodes them, admits corrupt bytes under another exact key, quarantines on decode failure, then proves lookup denial and zero bytes after reset
result: Corrupt catalog payloads cannot reach shadow replay or publication; focused target-reuse and realm matrices passed
